headline_draft: Claude Code compiler improvements: Agent map visualization, permissions dialog, improved telemetry in VSCode
summary: Claude Code shipped a series of developer experience improvements in the week of September 20–21, 2026, including an agent map footer pill in VSCode that shows all sub-agents in a session with per-agent transcripts and stop controls. The update also added a Hooks dialog in the command menu for viewing and editing hooks (user, project, and local settings), improved first-party sessions with telemetry disabled, and batched telemetry row optimization. These changes make it easier for PMs and developers to see and control agent orchestration, especially in complex multi-agent workflows.
why_pm: These are UX enhancements for agentic engineering—the pattern PMs will increasingly adopt. An agent map is a new UI primitive for reasoning about distributed agent systems. If you're building products with agents, watch Claude Code's UX choices as a template for how to make agent flows transparent and controllable.
key_facts: Agent map footer pill shows all sub-agents in a session with read-only transcripts
Hooks dialog added to command menu (view, add, edit, remove hooks)
Telemetry now batches rows and serves only built-in plugins
Improved first-party sessions with telemetry disabled
VSCode plugin interface refinements as of Sept 20–21, 2026
quotes: Added an agent map: an N agents footer pill opens a map of the session's sub-agents with per-agent cards, Stop agent, and read-only transcripts

headline_draft: OpenAI retires Custom GPTs, migrates users to plugins as GPT Store strategy shifts
summary: OpenAI quietly closed Custom GPT creation and publishing on September 19, 2026, restricting creation and public deployment to business accounts only. With 3 million GPTs in total but only 159,000 public and active, the policy fundamentally reframes the three-way platform choice: OpenAI's plugin model versus Anthropic's Claude Skills versus Google's Gemini Gems. The move signals OpenAI's shift away from user-generated content toward managed, vetted plugins with reusable instructions and connected apps. This leaves teams that relied on Custom GPTs to either migrate to plugins or switch platforms.
why_pm: As a PM evaluating AI agent customization platforms, you need to understand which ecosystem you're actually betting on. This retirement fundamentally changes the playbook for building personalized agents on ChatGPT and raises the question: is plugin adoption the future, or should teams prototype on Claude Skills or Gemini instead?
key_facts: OpenAI closed Custom GPT creation as of August 16, 2026 for most users
3 million GPTs exist total; only 159,000 are public and active
Migration path to plugins (reusable instructions + connected apps) now primary offering
Restricts creation to business accounts and workspace admins
